title: Wave | BrainVault Mint for Hermes: full demo
summary: A 2½-minute silent, captioned walkthrough of the Wave | BrainVault Mint plugin for Hermes Agent: set up Wave Wallet Mint and sign in to Wave Web, save and mint one private memory card, turn a whole page into 8 cards minted with one approval, then recall a memory from the vault on Theta. Wallet balances and emails are blurred.
how_to_use: Times are seconds from the start of the full video (accurate to about half a second). Use the step whose start <= current time < end to explain what's on screen. The short 68-second version (wave-brainvault-mint-hermes-demo-short.mp4) shows the same flow faster and doesn't follow these times.

chapters.title: Part 3: A whole page, one approval

steps.caption: Connecting
steps.explain: Hermes Agent (the AI agent app by Nous Research) is opening the Wave | BrainVault Mint page and connecting to Wave.
steps.narration: Hi, I'm Wavey. I'll walk you through it.

steps.caption: Wave | BrainVault Mint: memory you own.
steps.explain: The plugin's name and what it does: memory you own, minted to your own wallet on the Theta blockchain, readable by you and your Hermes.
steps.narration: This is Wave BrainVault Mint: memory you own, on Theta.

steps.caption: Install Wave Wallet Mint in Chrome and open your wallet. Your keys stay in the wallet.
steps.explain: Wave Wallet Mint is Wave's Chrome wallet extension (download at oswave.io/mint). The viewer installs it and opens it. The wallet keeps the keys; Hermes and the plugin never get them.
steps.narration: First, the wallet. This is Wave Wallet Mint, a Chrome extension. Your keys stay inside it, and nothing else ever gets them.

steps.caption: Your wallet on Theta mainnet. It pays for minting in TFUEL.
steps.explain: The wallet is on Theta mainnet. Minting a memory card costs a small network fee in TFUEL, Theta's gas token, paid from this wallet. The balance is blurred in the video.
steps.narration: It's on Theta mainnet. Minting fees are paid in TFUEL from here.

steps.caption: Sign in to Wave Web with Wave Wallet Mint. Free, no transaction.
steps.explain: Wave Web (web.oswave.io) is where cards are minted. Signing in uses the wallet to sign a message, which is free and isn't a transaction.
steps.narration: Now signing in to Wave Web with the wallet. That's just a signature: free, and not a transaction.

steps.caption: Wave | BrainVault Mint lives in Hermes: paired with your wallet, private by default.
steps.explain: The Wave | BrainVault Mint page inside Hermes. It's paired with the wallet once (Hermes gets a decrypt-only agent key that can't sign or spend and can be revoked in the wallet). Memories are private by default.
steps.narration: Here's the plugin's own page inside Hermes. It's paired with your wallet once, and everything is private by default.

steps.caption: Teach Hermes something worth keeping. It's saved on this computer first.
steps.explain: The viewer tells Hermes a fact worth keeping. Hermes saves it on this computer straight away, so recall works instantly even before anything is minted.
steps.narration: Teaching Hermes a fact. It's saved on your computer right away, so recall works before anything is minted.

steps.caption: Send it to Wave: one card, about 1.2 TFUEL, Readable by Me + Hermes.
steps.explain: Send to Wave opens Wave Web's Quick mint for one card, about 1.2 TFUEL. 'Readable by: Me + Hermes' means the card is encrypted so only the owner's wallet and this paired Hermes can open it.
steps.narration: Send to Wave makes one card, about 1.2 TFUEL, readable only by you and your paired Hermes.

steps.caption: Sync: Hermes reads the card from Theta and opens it with its own key.
steps.explain: Sync: Hermes reads the card back from the Theta blockchain, opens it with its own agent key and checks its fingerprint. This is how a new computer gets its memories back.
steps.narration: Sync reads the card back from Theta, opens it with Hermes's own key and checks its fingerprint. That's how a new computer gets your memories back.

steps.caption: Paste a whole page. Hermes turns it into 8 private memory cards and estimates the cost.
steps.explain: Paste a whole web page or document. The plugin turns it into 8 clean memory cards (one idea per card, private by default) and shows the estimated TFUEL cost.
steps.narration: Now a whole page at once. Paste it in, and Hermes splits it into 8 private cards, one idea each, with the cost shown up front.

steps.caption: Review and edit them, then Send selected to Wave. Nothing is spent yet.
steps.explain: The viewer reviews and edits the cards, then picks Send selected to Wave. Nothing is spent at this step.
steps.narration: You can review and edit every card first. Sending them to Wave doesn't spend anything yet.

steps.caption: Quick mint on Wave Web: Readable by Me + Hermes on this computer.
steps.explain: Wave Web's Quick mint lists all the cards, the cost, and 'Readable by: Me + Hermes on this computer'.
steps.narration: Wave Web's Quick mint lists all 8 cards and the total cost, readable by you and this Hermes.

steps.caption: One Wave Wallet Mint approval. The plugin never sees your wallet key.
steps.explain: One approval in Wave Wallet Mint mints all the cards. Private cards are encrypted in the wallet before they reach the chain. The plugin never sees the wallet key.
steps.narration: One approval in Wave Wallet Mint covers all of them. Private cards are encrypted in the wallet before they reach the chain.

steps.caption: All 8 cards minted in 1 transaction on Theta (v3:327 to v3:334).
steps.explain: All 8 cards were minted in one transaction on Theta (card numbers v3:327 to v3:334).
steps.narration: Done: all 8 cards minted in a single transaction on Theta, cards v3:327 to v3:334.

steps.caption: Sync: 9 on chain, opened with this Hermes's own key, every fingerprint checked.
steps.explain: Sync again: 9 cards are now on chain, opened with this Hermes's own key, and every fingerprint checked.
steps.narration: Sync again: 9 cards on chain, each opened with this Hermes's own key and fingerprint-checked.

steps.caption: Ask “when is the demo due?” Hermes recalls it from your vault on Theta.
steps.explain: The viewer asks 'when is the demo due?' and Hermes answers from the memory vault on Theta, so the memory works on any paired computer.
steps.narration: Now the payoff. Asking 'when is the demo due?' and Hermes answers from your vault on Theta. Pair another computer and it remembers there too.

steps.caption: Built to be trusted
steps.explain: Safety points: the plugin never signs, never mints and never sees the wallet key; cards are private by default, encrypted to you and your Hermes; seed phrases, keys and passwords are blocked from becoming cards; every card read from Theta is fingerprint-checked; it's open source (MIT).
steps.narration: Built to be trusted: it never signs, mints or sees your key, it blocks seed phrases, and it's open source.

steps.caption: Get it on GitHub · oswave.io/hermes
steps.explain: Get it at github.com/xBuildyTeam/wave-os-hermes. More at oswave.io/hermes. Hermes puts your agent in any browser; Wave puts your agent's memory on any machine.
steps.narration: That's it! Get it free on GitHub, and ask me anything about installing or pairing it.
